Feature: Is there an overt marker for the absolutive?
Comment: There is no explicit marker for the absolutive case.
curated_comment: Baram Thangmi (bara1357, Trans-Himalayan, Nepal) shows ergative alignment documented in Dhakal (2014). The ergative marker is -e/-i, which is syncretic with the instrumental marker (GB409_24=1), while comitative uses -səŋ. All 24 features verified against Dhakal (2014). GB409_22=1 confirmed: a NOM-ACC pattern can emerge with highly affected/definite objects (p.54), constituting additional conditioning. GB409_15 citation in original xlsx (pp.63-64) covers clause syntax rather than agentivity, but the value 1 is retained as no agentivity split is documented. Glottocode bara1357 is correct; the previously proposed than1259 (Thangmi) corresponds to a different Thangmi variety (Dolakha/Sindhupalchok), not Baram Thangmi.

Feature: Is ergative alignment of flagging conditioned by any other factor?
Comment: Ergative marking is conditioned by differential object marking: when the object is highly affected/definite, the NOM-ACC pattern can emerge; the ergative marker is -e/-i (also used as instrumental). This split is based on transitivity scale / object properties.

Feature: Are the ergative and the instrumental/comitative expressed by the same marker?
Comment: The ergative marker -e/-i is also the instrumental marker. Comitative uses a different marker (-səŋ). ERG=INST confirmed.
